settings.comment_skipAudits: charset is skipped for a TOOLING reason, not a site one. It requires Lighthouse's MainDocumentContent gatherer, which calls Network.getResponseBody; on this site's 300-630 KB HTML documents Chrome evicts the body from its network buffer and the call fails with a protocol error. The audit then errors, which makes the WHOLE best-practices category score NaN and fails the error-level categories:best-practices assertion. It has flapped between 0 and 6 URLs per run since well before anyone looked at it. Every page does declare <meta charSet="utf-8"> (Next emits it) — verified against production — so skipping the audit loses no real signal, while keeping the rest of best-practices gated. Revisit if the documents ever get materially smaller.
settings.comment_maxWaitForLoad: Content-heavy detail pages (e.g. a thesis) can exceed Lighthouse's default 45s load cap under simulated mobile throttling; an incomplete gather then reports present metadata (meta-description) as missing. 60s lets the audit complete and reflect reality. Real mobile perf is still tracked by the categories:performance warn assertion.

assertMatrix.comment: All audited URLs. SEO + canonical live in the auth-excluding entry below: noindex utility pages (e.g. /auth/login) legitimately fail is-crawlable and must not be held to a public-SEO score.
Indexable content pages only — everything except /auth/* (login/signup are noindex by design, so a public-SEO threshold and canonical assertion are false signals there).
